newsitem.title: USA: New U.S. health guidelines on Alzheimers, elderly.
newsitem.headline: New U.S. health guidelines on Alzheimers, elderly.

text.p: Mental impairment is not a "normal" part of ageing and many cases of dementia can be treated, according to U.S. health guidelines released on Wednesday.
Even when the problem cannot be cured, such as Alzheimer's disease, early diagnosis is still advisable.

"Early recognition of Alzheimer's disease or identification of other types of dementias can prevent costly and inappropriate treatment and give patients and family members time to address the complex financial, legal and medical conditions these conditions present," said Paul Costa of the National Institute on Ageing, and the co-chair of the panel that drew up the guidelines.
The clinical practice guidelines are the last in a series drawn up by the Agency for Health Care Policy and Research, part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

About one in five apparent cases of dementia are treatable, due to such disorders as depression or drug interaction, which is a particular problem among older people taking several medications for chronic conditions.

Yet many people, including some health care professionals, regard such symptoms as a difficulty absorbing new information, problems in handling complex tasks or trouble with spatial orientation as sad but normal parts of ageing.
But according to the guidelines, they are instead signals that a doctor should be consulted. If Alzheimer's is suspected, the elderly person should be followed carefully.
